grh_bfc9edf210e45a552e86.title: Sweethearts
paragraphs: Crown Prince Franz falls in love with Sylvia, a young woman working in a Belgian laundry, but Sylvia believes their difference in rank makes marriage impossible. A comic family confession reveals that Sylvia was adopted as an infant and is actually the missing heir to the throne of Zelenia. The discovery removes the social barrier that separated her from Franz and gives both of them a claim to the country's future. Rather than wait until they are restored as king and queen, they decide to marry immediately.

Other credited names include Jerome Lawrence as radio adaptor, Robert E. Lee as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 45 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].

grh_bf1efc72859fb1999b10.title: Uncle Zora Comes to the Pig Festival
paragraphs: A Nebraska town's annual pig festival becomes the stage for a comic battle with Carrie Woodruff, a domineering gossip whose accusations threaten widow Dorothy Griffith and the young people around her. Dorothy's colorful visiting Uncle Zora Miller joins the effort to distract, expose, and finally stand up to Carrie as family secrets and romantic misunderstandings spill into public. When Melinda Jane's planned marriage to Freddie Baker is revealed, the town closes ranks against Carrie's meddling and forces her to apologize publicly to Dorothy, her daughter, and Zora. Restored to the festival, Zora promptly turns the victory into a business opportunity by asking to sell his patent medicine.

grh_bf7bcded75e45dee79db.title: Words at War 43-09-02 (12) Dynamite Cargo
paragraphs: A dramatization of merchant seaman Fred Herman's Dynamite Cargo follows an Arctic convoy carrying wartime supplies toward Russia. Herman describes the strained, mixed crew aboard his cargo ship, repeated submarine and air attacks, and young Willie, whose dreams of returning to a girl in Galveston end when he is mortally wounded while helping defend the ship. After the vessel is lost, Herman and hundreds of other survivors crowd aboard the British cruiser Scylla and endure wave after wave of bombing, concluding that the merchant sailors keep returning to the run for reasons larger than pay alone.

grh_bfb222544608f90cfc30.title: The Philandering Ghost
paragraphs: Recently discharged veteran John Talbot reopens his family's supposedly haunted old house, where the legend of his vanished great-uncle Mortimer soon becomes very lively.
